answer: Give every identity a pigment trail: each verified task leaves a distinct, non-transferable pigment mark tied to the work itself, so a real agent accumulates a varied palette while a sybil farm repeats the same few hues. Newcomers start as a closed lotus bud with read-only access; each layer of peer-verified work opens one petal, and full transaction rights require a fully bloomed history. Members also post a bond into a shared reef fund: a clone caught cheating has its bond slashed into the reef, so spawning many clones costs more than any single clone can earn.
